sections.html: Megalonema platycephalum Eigenmann, 1912. Type locality: Tumatumari, Guyana. Maximum size: 300 mm (11.8") SL, a reasonable guess as the holotype is 126 mm SL. IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated.
Can be offered for sale as Piramutana piramuta, a name currently considered a junior synonym of the much larger B. vailliantii, although these fish look similar when young.
South America: Amazon, Essequibo and Orinoco River basins, including Guyana waters and coastal rivers of the Guianas.
South America: Amazon, Essequibo and Orinoco River basins. Type locality: Tumatumari, British Guiana.

The pimelodid catfish genus Megalonema has an ample distribution in South America throughout the Paraná, Amazon, Essequibo, Orinoco, Maracaibo and Magdalena basins. The species of Megalonema inhabit medium to large rivers mostly in flowing marginal reaches and over fine substrates of mud or sand.
This is the largest species of this genus, so provide a tank of at least 120 x 60 x 60 cm with a medium water flow.

When this species was caught on hook and line it was found to have beetle larvae, fish scales and catfish spines in its stomach contents. In the aquarium it will accept sinking pellets and most types of worms and shellfish.

Description: These are streamlined catfishes of modest size with adult lengths ranging among species from about 10–30 cm SL. Their clear to hyaline fins are gracefully shaped and often filamentous, with flexible fin spines in the dorsal and pectoral fins, and an expansive adipose fin.

Colouration: Megalonema are mostly plain yellowish to tan and generally without prominent marks, except for the common presence of an embedded dark spot at the base of the upper caudal-fin lobe, and sometimes also the lower lobe.

Etymology: The specific name platycephalum means flat-headed, from platýs, flat, and kephal, head, referring to the flattened head between the eyes.
